text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.5% today, continuing a sharp two-week decline of over 10% that began right after the company reported earnings on November 5th. The stock has been trending downward since that announcement, suggesting investors reacted negatively to the quarterly results despite the company operating in an environment where US oil is trading at $99.64 per barrel—a reasonably healthy price for an oil major.

The broader oil market remains stable with global crude near $107 per barrel, but geopolitical risks haven't intensified dramatically in the past few days. The recent comments from the U.S. Secretary of State about stalled Iran negotiations typically wouldn't trigger such a consistent selloff on their own. This suggests the market's focus has been primarily on ConocoPhillips' own financial performance and guidance rather than external energy market factors.
